age.evidence: Experiments were performed on adult (10 -17 weeks old) male and female 129S6/SvEv mice

sex.evidence: Experiments were performed on adult (10 -17 weeks old) male and female 129S6/SvEv mice

dosing.evidence: We tested the effect of the psychedelic 1-(2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodophenyl)-2-aminopropane (DOI) (0.5 mg/kg, i.p.)... Drugs were dissolved in saline (0.9%).
we evaluated the effect of ... the psychedelic LSD (0.24 mg/kg, i.p.)

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were housed on a 12 h light/dark cycle... except during behavioral testing which took place during the light cycle

assays.assay_description: Magnet ear-tagged mice placed in plastic container surrounded by coil; head-twitches detected via signal processing + CNN-based deep learning classifier; 30-min recording post-injection.

application_type.evidence: After treatment with DOI (0.5 mg/kg) or vehicle... All drugs or vehicle were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_restrain.evidence: ear-tagged mice were placed inside a plastic container

food_restriction.evidence: food and water ad libitum, except during behavioral testing

water_restriction.evidence: food and water ad libitum, except during behavioral testing

time_to_assay.evidence: After treatment with DOI (0.5 mg/kg) or vehicle, ear-tagged mice were placed inside a plastic container... Testing lasted 30 min

outcomes.summary: DOI (0.5 mg/kg) significantly increased head-twitch counts during the 30 min post-injection period in both male and female mice, with no sex differences observed.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way repeated measures ANOVA F[3,20]=40.00, p<0.001; vehicle vs DOI F[1,20]=212.3, p<0.001; sex effect F[1,20]=1.48, p>0.05
outcomes.evidence: Total head-twitch counts were also increased upon DOI administration (vehicle vs DOI, F [1,20] = 212.3, p < 0.001; sex-related differences, F [1,20] = 1.48, p > 0.05)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time-course showing head-twitch (HTR) counts on 15-min blocks

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: signal was also processed using a deep learning-based protocol based on scalograms... convolutional neural network (CNN) employed was trained using head-twitch and non-head-twitch events

E1_environment_type.evidence: placed inside a plastic container surrounded by a coil

D4_baseline.evidence: After treatment with DOI... mice were placed inside a plastic container

assays.assay_description: Acoustic startle and PPI in SR-LAB startle chambers; 5-min acclimation + 65 trials (~30 min total); startle amplitude and %PPI measured under up to four parameter sets (varying background, prepulse/pulse intensity and duration, ISI), with DOI, LSD, M100,907, apomorphine, and SKF-82,958.

application_type.evidence: All drugs or vehicle were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.), except apomorphine, which as administered subcutaneously (s.c.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were habituated to the testing room at least 1 h prior to the start of the experiment (room habituation only, not apparatus pre-exposure)

setup_restrain.evidence: SR-LAB Startle Response System (PPI startle chambers with body-restraint tubes per rubric definition)

food_restriction.evidence: food and water ad libitum, except during behavioral testing

water_restriction.evidence: food and water ad libitum, except during behavioral testing

time_to_assay.evidence: treatment or vehicle was administered to subjects immediately prior to testing

sample_size.evidence: n = 10 mice per group (Figs 3,5,6,8,9); n = 9-10 (Figs 4,7,10); n = 7-8 (Fig 13); n = 4 mice per group (Fig 14)

outcomes.summary: DOI (0.5 mg/kg) increased %PPI in male 129S6/SvEv mice in 3 of 4 paradigm conditions and altered startle amplitude; the %PPI augmentation was blocked by M100,907 (1 mg/kg). In females, DOI increased %PPI more weakly without affecting startle amplitude. LSD (0.24 mg/kg) also increased %PPI in males without affecting startle. Apomorphine (5 mg/kg) and SKF-82,958 (0.5 mg/kg) decreased %PPI as expected.
outcomes.evidence: DOI... increased %PPI in three out of four PPI conditions in male mice -an effect that was prevented by M100,907. In female mice, DOI increased %PPI without affecting startle amplitude... apomorphine and SKF-82,958 induced decreases in %PPI.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Comparison of pulse-only trials before vs after the session is a between-trial-block comparison, not within-session temporal binning

B4_ethological.evidence: PPI startle magnitude is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B6_cognitive.evidence: PPI is a sensorimotor gating reflex, not learning/memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: SR-LAB Startle Response System (commercial startle transducer, not behavioural classifier)

B8_multivariate.evidence: Pearson correlations and ANOVA only; no multivariate dimensionality reduction

D1_continuity.evidence: Each session lasted about a total of 30 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each session lasted about a total of 30 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: single PPI session per assay (Behavioral tests were separated by at least a 1 week wash-out period)

D4_baseline.evidence: treatment or vehicle was administered to subjects immediately prior to testing

D5_followup.evidence: no testing >=24h after dosing within this assay

judge_notes: Merged all PPI variants (4 paradigm conditions, DOI, LSD, M100,907 antagonist, apomorphine, SKF-82,958, both sexes) into a single PPI assay per rubric — same paradigm/apparatus with different drug and parameter manipulations.
Kept HTR and PPI as two separate assays.
B1 for PPI scored as 2-3 (startle amplitude + %PPI = 2 measures) rather than candidate glm's 1.
B2 for PPI scored 0: the before/after pulse-only comparison is between-block not within-session minute-binned temporal dynamics; rejected qwen's 'Yes'.
setup_restrain=yes for PPI (SR-LAB restraint tubes per rubric).
Food/water restriction set to 'during' based on explicit 'ad libitum except during behavioral testing'.
DOI outcome direction across full PPI assay set as 'mixed' (DOI increases PPI but apomorphine/SKF decrease — same assay contains opposing effects across compounds).
